title: Testing the Racing Game
author: Harlan_42
selftext: When I am testing my game, [www.stockarjr.com](http://www.stockarjr.com) I use a screen recorder to capture all the action, also to review the debug screen and check the racing.  At 60 frames a second it is hard to see the details go by so fast.  In a video editor I can go frame by frame and grab screenshots for Claude to explain.  And he's got plenty of explaining to do.

comments.author: SupMekBots
comments.body:
Haha, Claude's got some explaining to do!!  
  
Do you send it a few consecutive frames so it can follow how the issue develops?

replies.author: Harlan_42
replies.body: I playback in video editor on full screen and take screen shots to post.  Then write a little narrative.  Been working on pitting for my race game with a bunch of things going wrong, I can identify them and sometimes find others, hence bunch.  I traced back a stoppage to three issues and now am about to test the resolution.

replies.author: SupMekBots
replies.body:
I see, yeah I also did similar thing, where I basically asked Codex to review the animation, whether it contains glitches or not, and even edit that specific glitched frame using imagegen skill  :D

Btw, I'm also working on [Super Mekabots](https://supermekabots.com), a browser mecha card game. If you feel like trying something different sometime, I'd welcome your thoughts on how it plays!

replies.author: Harlan_42
replies.body: Checked out your app, and as a problem solver I usually only see problems, that is me.  I can provide the good or the bad, but in both cases, it is only my opinion.  Also, if I do provide advice, it is only as an alternative for you to decide should be clear.  You tell me, would you like some feedback, or let sleeping dogs lay.
